summary: Weekly POC sync focused on onboarding progress, access setup for VPC and staging, and early tuning results. Discussed a performance/cost tradeoff between hosted and Dedicated, next steps for peering and a 10k inference benchmark. Agreed on deliverables and timelines for final results review.
topics: Onboarding status and access (VPC peering, IAM, KMS)
Staging endpoint readiness and initial perf results
Quantization / tuning notes and expected cost impact
Next steps and scheduling final results review
transcript:
00:00:00 - Daniel: okay good morning everyone, thanks for joining, we've got 45 minutes; quick roll call - Daniel Park from Redwood, Maya Chen SE, Priya from CSM
00:00:12 - Laura: hi Laura here, CTO at NexaHealth, Ravi and Sofia on the line as well
00:00:20 - Ravi: hey all
00:00:22 - Sofia: hi
00:00:30 - Daniel: awesome, agenda — onboarding status, access, early perf numbers that Maya has from last night's run, then next steps, is that good?
00:00:38 - Laura: yes, sounds good
00:00:45 - Maya: quick note, transcript might have a couple typos, I ran the 1k sample yesterday then a larger 5k overnight; will go over numbers
00:00:52 - Daniel: perfect, Maya you wanna kick off with the staging endpoint readiness?
00:01:00 - Maya: sure, so we validated the model artifact and pushed the variant q4_128 (quantized 4-bit) to the staging pool; we saw stable startup, KV cache warmup is working, latency median around 120ms on 8k context for single-shot requests in the pushed environment, p95 about 320ms during the brief load test
00:01:22 - Ravi: hmm 120ms median is promising; what hardware was that on?
00:01:26 - Maya: that's on Dedicated g5x2 equivalent nodes (we ran on the POC pool we reserved) — we used auto-batching disabled for that run to measure single-request latency
00:01:40 - Sofia: just to confirm, is this in our VPC or Redwood hosted? we still haven't completed peering on our side
00:01:48 - Daniel: good call, this run was on Redwood-managed staging with VPC access not yet peered; so network latency to your infra not included in those numbers
00:01:58 - Laura: okay so we need the peered numbers to understand end-to-end; Sofia any update on peering?
00:02:05 - Sofia: chatted with infra this morning, we have a tentative window on Tuesday 12/22, but I can try to move it earlier if needed. we need a small firewall rule change and the peering setup on Redwood side confirmed
00:02:18 - Maya: for the peering we sent a short runbook link in the POC folder — it lists required CIDR ranges, ports 443 for API plus 10250 for health checks etc, and KMS endpoints for encryption calls
00:02:30 - Ravi: can you paste that link in chat? sometimes these things expire
00:02:34 - Daniel: will paste after the call, yes
00:02:38 - Priya: I'll also share the onboarding checklist and who to ping if anything stalls
00:02:44 - 00:02:50 - Maya: jumping back to performance, when we enable batching with a small batch window (20ms) we saw throughput increases and cost per token lowered ~18% but median latency increased to ~170ms — there's the expected tradeoff
00:03:05 - Laura: what's the expected impact on token cost for our 10k-run? we need that to estimate monthly spend for the pilot
00:03:12 - Maya: rough numbers are in the spreadsheet: hosted baseline cost estimate $0.018 per 1k tokens, dedicated with q4 and batching we're estimating about $0.009 per 1k tokens but that's very workload dependent, I'll upload the exact calc
00:03:25 - Ravi: are we confident quantization won't reduce quality for our summarization task? we saw a small BLEU-style drop in a 50-sample test last week
00:03:33 - Maya: good question — we ran a 200-sample eval comparing fp16 vs q4_128; average quality delta was minor, some edge cases had hallucinations increased slightly. We have a suggested fall back policy: keep an fp16 variant for critical routes and route non-critical background jobs to q4 to save cost
00:03:49 - Tom: from security perspective I want to make sure audit logs and KMS usage are recorded; do you have SOC2 artifacts?
00:03:58 - Daniel: yes, we have SOC2 and ISO docs; I'll drop the security pack link. For KMS, we support customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated via our KMS integration; for hosted you can opt-in for CMK in Dedicated plans
00:04:12 - Tom: and is the audit log retention configurable? our compliance needs 1 year of immutable logs
00:04:18 - Maya: we can retain at least 365 days with the audit add-on; and we can export to your SIEM — we'll capture token-level traces only as hashes for PII reduction per the runbook
00:04:30 - Laura: good. back to access, Ravi will run the 10k inference battery once peering is done. any gotchas for him? keys, endpoint names?
00:04:40 - Maya: you'll get a staging API URL and a service account key. For VPC peering the endpoint is internal-only, so you'll use the private DNS name. We also recommend using RBAC service accounts we've created for the POC (we shared ARNs in the onboarding doc)
00:04:58 - Ravi: ok, I saw the service account but didn't have permission to view the KMS keys yet — can we get that unlocked?
00:05:04 - Daniel: noted — Priya will follow up with admin invite and tell the infra team to grant kms:view and kms:encrypt to the service account
00:05:13 - Priya: will do, I can send the IAM policy snippet after the call
00:05:19 - 00:05:28 - Maya: quick note on the 5k run last night: p95 spiked to 520ms during concurrency bursts because we didn't have proper prefix caching enabled for multi-turn flows; enabling prefix/KV cache brought p95 down to ~340ms on subsequent tests
00:05:40 - Laura: multi-turn chat is important for our patient summarization use case, so prefix cache is critical
00:05:46 - Maya: agreed, and that's part of our Optimize recommendations. we'll provide the cache config and how it affects memory and throughput
00:05:55 - 00:06:05 - Ravi: about fallbacks, if Dedicated capacity is exhausted do you auto-failover to hosted? we need predictable behavior for peak times
00:06:11 - Daniel: we have routing policies; for the pilot we've recommended a canary with fallback to a slightly smaller model on Hosted or another Dedicated pool. we'll document latencies for those fallback paths so you can plan SLOs
00:06:24 - Laura: what about encryption in transit — TLS standards? we've seen some vendors use older ciphers
00:06:30 - Tom: yes TLS 1.2 vs 1.3 question
00:06:33 - Maya: we support TLS 1.2 and 1.3, default is 1.3, and we can provide cipher lists; we also do mutual TLS for Private deployments if you want cert-based auth
00:06:45 - 00:07:00 - Daniel: OK moving to the cost question again: the spreadsheet caveat is that your prompt length distribution matters — Ravi, can you share 1 week of production traces or a synthetic distribution so we can refine the estimate?
00:07:12 - Ravi: I'll anonymize and drop a sample later today; probably a 5-10% sample of requests is fine
00:07:18 - Maya: perfect, that will help us tune batch windows and quant profiles. on the tuning front, we recommend q4 with selective fp16 on regen routes; also suggest caching of frequent prefixes and using a 30ms batching window for async routes
00:07:33 - Laura: what's the effort to run an A/B between q4 and fp16 for us? we need to measure end-user visible regressions
00:07:40 - Maya: we'll help set up a dual-route config in the staging cluster; you'll be able to send traffic split 10/90, we capture metrics and a sample of outputs for manual review. should be 2-3 days of setup plus your evaluation time
00:07:52 - 00:08:10 - Sofia: if we do that, does that require extra capacity or can we use the same Dedicated pool?
00:08:14 - Maya: small overhead for running two model variants, but we can hot-swap variants on the same nodes if they share the same architecture; if they're different (e.g., fp16 big vs q4 small) it might require separate pools — we'll include sizing guidance in the proposal
00:08:30 - Daniel: action item: I'll put two example configs in the pricing doc: one single-variant Dedicated baseline, and one mixed variant with fallback; both with estimated costs for 100k requests/day
00:08:42 - Laura: great. one more compliance ask — data residency, we need logs and traces to remain in us-east-1 — is that supported?
00:08:50 - Maya: yes we can pin region for Dedicated and for Private; for hosted we can request regional tenancy but Dedicated gives you the strongest guarantee
00:08:59 - Tom: on audit logs, can we get a sample of the log format? field names, timestamps, user IDs?
00:09:05 - Daniel: yes, I'll attach a sample log JSON in the security pack
00:09:10 - 00:09:25 - Maya: to summarize technical to-dos: enable KV/prefix caching config, run the 10k via peered staging, collect output quality diffs for q4 vs fp16, and run the A/B with 10% traffic if possible
00:09:36 - Ravi: sounds good; question — you mentioned earlier the p95 520ms spike, do you have guidance on burst smoothing?
00:09:43 - Maya: yes, use request shaping + token budget per route, and set a soft queue to keep latency SLOs, plus auto-bursting policy for Dedicated if you have spare commit headroom
00:09:56 - Laura: scheduling: can we do final results review the week of 12/28? execs are available for a short demo on 12/30
00:10:04 - Daniel: yes we'll aim for that; we'll lock in after we see the 10k results
00:10:09 - 00:10:20 - Priya: I'll share the calendar invite for the 12/30 exec demo placeholder and a follow-up for the final results review
00:10:30 - Maya: small note — we saw one transcription artifact in the demo logs where 'KV cache' got transcribed as 'K V cash' in the last meeting, sorry for the joke, but just flagging transcription quirk
00:10:41 - 00:11:00 - Laura: ok no more points from us, Tom has one quick security question about key rotation frequency and whether Redwood enforces automatic rotation
00:11:08 - Tom: yes this is for our audit checklist
00:11:12 - Maya: we support automatic rotation for service-managed keys on a 90-day cadence; for customer-managed keys rotation is controlled by you, but we can trigger reminders and help with the rotation process
00:11:25 - Tom: perfect that's fine
00:11:30 - Daniel: wrapping up — recap: Daniel to send pricing and SLO examples, Maya to upload tuned configs and perf notes, Priya to handle IAM invite and calendar events, Sofia to finalize peering window, Ravi to run the 10k and post results. we'll plan final review 12/28-12/31 with exec demo 12/30 tentative
00:11:55 - Laura: thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity
00:12:00 - Daniel: thanks, we'll follow up in email and with the shared drive artifacts
00:12:05 - (call ends)
